title: Share the Charge
summary: Deliver exact charges to an experiment by touching identical metal spheres together, using as few touches as you can.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: After winning, the student can plan a sequence of contacts between identical conductors, knows the total charge is unchanged by touching, and knows it only changes when charge escapes to the ground.

levels.title: Share and share alike
levels.adds: Baseline: three identical spheres on insulating stands. Touch pairs together to reach the goal charges.
hints: When two identical spheres touch, what happens to their charges?
They share their combined charge equally, so each ends up with the average.
Work backwards from the goal: which touch could have produced those numbers?

levels.title: Opposites meet
levels.adds: New idea: some spheres are negative. Touching a + and a − sphere cancels part of both before the rest is shared.
hints: Add the two charges with their signs first, then halve.
The total in the lab never changes when spheres touch: check it before and after.
A neutral sphere is a handy way to split a charge in half.

levels.title: One eighth
levels.adds: Harder: only one sphere has a goal, and it is a small fraction of the starting charge. Plan a chain of halvings.
hints: Each touch with a neutral sphere halves a charge.
To get one eighth you need three halvings in a row.
Use the sphere you just charged as the one to touch next.

levels.title: The leaky lab
levels.adds: New idea: you can touch a sphere to the Earth. Charge flows away, so the lab's total is no longer conserved.
hints: Compare the lab's total now with the total the goal needs.
Touching spheres together can never change the total, so something has to carry charge away.
Earthing a sphere sets it to zero: plan so only the charge you want to lose is on it.

misconceptions: Charge is used up or created when bodies touch
Touching moves ALL the charge onto the other sphere
Total charge is conserved even when a sphere is connected to the ground
